properties.name: PREDICTIONS, registered before any run (2026-10-29): increment 8, the pilot's memories answered again under a reading budget of 12 KB and 36 KB (the notes file is 84 KB), plus traceability and structuring-against-using
properties.source: Claude (this session), before any budgeted run
properties.statement:
SETUP: the pilot's finished memories are kept as they are: the notes file (84,475 bytes, 298 lines) and the reflow2 design (422 nodes). A fresh Sonnet agent answers the same 25 questions, but every byte it reads from memory counts against a budget, through a reader that refuses once it is spent: notes by grep or line ranges, reflow2 by read-only queries. Two budgets: 12,000 and 36,000 bytes. The summary arm (9 KB) is not re-run; it fits either budget, so its pilot score stands. Scored blind against the same key. Traceability (c) is scored separately on all arms' answers: can a person, from the memory alone, point to the records that support the answer and see how they connect (0, ½, 1 each).

STRUCTURING AGAINST USING (d), already measured from the pilot's costs: structuring (the six writing rounds) A 386k tokens / 8 min, B 478k / 10 min, C 1,082k / 49 min; using (one answering round) A 57k / 1 min, B 98k / 1.6 min, C 164k / 3.4 min.

PREDICTIONS:
P6. At 12 KB, reflow2 beats the notes file by at least 3 points: a query returns the record and its links, while grep returns long lines around a word.
P7. At 36 KB, the gap narrows to at most 2 points either way.
P8. Both budgeted arms score below their unbudgeted pilot scores (25 and 24.5).
P9. Traceability: reflow2 scores at least 5 points higher than the notes file, and the summary lowest.
P10. Using costs: under the same budget the two arms' answering tokens are within 30% of each other; reflow2's large cost is in structuring, not in using.
